articles.title: Warning Issued Over Broken Glass at Dogford Park
articles.excerpt: Dog owners are advised to exercise caution at Dogford Park due to broken glass found near the Rochdale Road entrance. The area has been partially cleared, but hazards remain.
articles.content_html:
A warning has been issued for dog owners regarding broken glass at Dogford Park. The glass is located on the grass and path area around the Rochdale Road entrance, near the traffic lights.

Local residents have reported that they have picked up as much broken glass as possible, but many shards remain scattered throughout the area. Dog owners are advised to be vigilant while walking their pets in the park.

The presence of broken glass poses a risk to both dogs and their owners, and it is recommended that visitors to the park take extra care when using this entrance.

Anyone who visits Dogford Park should remain cautious and consider using alternative routes until the area can be fully cleared of hazards.

articles.title: Lift at Derker Tram Stop Out of Service Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers travelling towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
A lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 8:14am on Wednesday, 12 August 2026, and will remain unavailable until further notice.

Customers travelling towards Manchester can access the Manchester-bound platform via a ramp from Cromford Street. Those travelling away from Manchester can use a ramp from Cromford Street and a track crossing to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by the disruption and has provided alternative access routes for passengers.

articles.excerpt: A recent Netwalk event around Hollingworth Lake in Littleborough attracted a mix of new and familiar faces, fostering connections and conversations in a scenic setting.
articles.content_html:
A recent Netwalk event took place around Hollingworth Lake in Littleborough, welcoming both new and familiar participants. The event, held on a sunny Wednesday, provided an opportunity for attendees to engage in conversations and build connections.

Participants enjoyed the scenic surroundings of the lake, which is known for its natural beauty. The event concluded with refreshments at the Woodlands Cafe, located next to the RSPCA centre, where attendees could continue their discussions over coffee.

Organisers expressed gratitude to everyone who attended, highlighting the positive atmosphere and the chance to network in a relaxed environment. Such events are designed to promote local business connections and community engagement.

The Netwalk series aims to encourage outdoor activity while fostering professional relationships among local businesses and residents. Further events are expected to be organised in the future, continuing to utilise the picturesque settings of the area.

articles.title: Private hire driver targeted near Littleborough Station
articles.excerpt: A private hire driver was targeted near Littleborough Station when an unknown man opened his car door, placed a dog and a bag inside, and attempted to smash a window. Police attended the scene.
articles.content_html:
A private hire driver was targeted near Littleborough Station on Monday evening. An unknown man opened the driver's car door, placed a dog and a bag inside, and then attempted to smash a window.

Police attended the scene following the incident. The driver has urged colleagues to keep their doors locked while working to ensure their safety.

The incident has raised concerns among local cab drivers, who are now more vigilant about their security measures while on duty.

Anyone with information can find Greater Manchester Police and Crimestoppers contact details at the end of this article.

articles.title: No trains between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria this week as replacement buses run
articles.excerpt: Passengers travelling between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are being advised to allow extra time this week, with trains replaced by buses from Monday 10 to Friday 14 August.
articles.content_html:
Rail passengers travelling between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are facing disruption this week, with no train service operating on the route from Monday 10 August to Friday 14 August 2026 because of planned engineering work.

Rail replacement buses are operating between Manchester Victoria and Rochdale. Passengers can use a direct replacement service or a stopping service calling at Moston, Mills Hill and Castleton. Travellers making the full journey between Rochdale and Manchester Victoria are advised to use the direct replacement bus where possible.

The disruption has prompted concern locally after passengers checking journeys discovered that their usual trains had been replaced. One post in the Rochdale Borough Noticeboard Facebook group said: ‘Just noticed there are no trains from Rochdale to Manchester this week, only replacement buses.’

The closure forms part of planned engineering work affecting services into and out of Manchester Victoria. Other Calder Valley services are operating to revised timetables, so passengers travelling beyond Rochdale should check their individual journey before setting off.

Replacement buses generally take longer than the normal rail journey and passengers should leave additional time, particularly during busy commuting periods. Anyone with onward connections is advised to check the latest timetable before travelling.

The disruption is currently scheduled to continue through Friday 14 August, with passengers advised to check National Rail or their train operator for the latest journey information before setting off.
